scope: Part 2 Sprint 2 — East corridor service-pattern reconstruction
principles: Do not collapse all Route 2 services into one path.
Priority Bus Route and Eastern Main Road patterns are distinct.
A named destination service does not automatically serve every settlement between endpoints.
Intermediate trip generation requires an ordered served-point pattern plus pickup/alighting permission.
Reverse direction remains independent unless separately supported.

evidence.claim: Route 2 maxis run along both the Priority Bus Route and Eastern Main Road from Port of Spain toward La Horquetta, Arima, Maloney, Sangre Grande and other east-west communities.
Direct Route 2 destination services include Arima, Maloney, La Horquetta and Sangre Grande, with short-drop fares also recognized along the corridor.
Documented 2021 short-drop points toward Port of Spain include D'Abadie, Five Rivers, Cane Farm/Tunapuna and Curepe.
City Gate has a La Horquetta/Maloney bay (Bay 4), corroborating destination-specific Route 2 service patterns rather than one generic eastbound route.
Direct Port of Spain to Sangre Grande maxi service exists; routing via Arima is an alternative, not proof that every Grande passenger must transfer in Arima.
Arima historically distinguishes Priority Bus Route maxi-taxis from Main Road maxi-taxis with separate stands, supporting distinct service-pattern classes.
Sangre Grande red-band maxi operations currently center on Brierley Street/Eastern Main Road.

proposedPatterns.notes: The short-drop fare ladder provides unusually useful evidence that these are usable intermediate points on Route 2 corridor service. Exact sub-patterns and stop permissions still need canonical mapping.
Do not infer every PBR community as a served stop until path/pickup behavior is established.
La Horquetta and Maloney share a City Gate bay in current reporting but are not assumed to have identical downstream patterns.
PBR pattern supported; historical official evidence distinguishes PBR and Main Road operations at Arima.
Do not fabricate exact intermediate communities yet; official historical evidence proves a distinct Main Road maxi class.
Direct service is established. Do not automatically insert Arima or Valencia as pickup points until direct-service stopping behavior is supported.
Arima-to-Grande service is established; Valencia lies on the Eastern Main Road corridor but its intermediate boarding role should remain a research lead until independently supported.
